locations.name: A tile painter's workshop, past closing

collaborator.gift: a scrap of a fado phrase, hummed onto a napkin

preShowChoices.label: Play it acoustic
preShowChoices.description: Strip it back. Let the room breathe.

preShowChoices.label: Invite Inês up for a duet
preShowChoices.description: One song, two voices, no rehearsal.

minigames.title: Soundcheck
minigames.introText: The house engineer waves you up. "Give me a level check — tap when the needle's hot."
minigames.outroText: "Clean signal, good levels," the engineer says. "You're set for tonight."
minigames.outroTextRough: "A little hot in places," the engineer shrugs, "but it'll read fine from the back."

minigames.title: Load-In
minigames.introText: Inês is already hauling amps up the fado house's narrow stairs. "Faster if we split the load."
minigames.outroText: Everything's in with time to spare. Inês nods, impressed despite herself.
minigames.outroTextRough: Half the gear's still on the sidewalk when the doors open — you finish mid-apology.

lis_arrival.speaker: narrator
lis_arrival.text: The train smelled like rain and rust. Lisbon waited, unbothered, terracotta roofs going gold in the last light.

choices.label: Get the gear off the train

lis_arrival_view.speaker: narrator
lis_arrival_view.text: A river the color of tin. Someone nearby hums the venue's name like it's a secret worth keeping.

lis_arrival_gear.speaker: narrator
lis_arrival_gear.text: The amp case is heavier every city. You don't say that out loud anymore.

lis_arrival_mira.speaker: mira
lis_arrival_mira.text: "I keep forgetting we're allowed to just... be here," Mira says, not quite a joke.

lis_loc_fado.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_fado.text: A voice cracks mid-note and holds anyway. The singer — Inês — catches your eye between verses.

lis_loc_fado_listen.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_fado_listen.text: You leave humming a melody that isn't yours yet.

lis_loc_fado_round.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_fado_round.text: The bartender remembers your face now. Small victories.

lis_loc_records.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_records.text: Crates of vinyl, dust like snow. Jun is already elbow-deep in the Brazilian section, grinning.

lis_loc_records_dig.speaker: jun
lis_loc_records_dig.text: "Listen to this bassline," Jun says, for the fourth record in a row.

lis_loc_records_wander.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_records_wander.text: You find a 7-inch with no label at all and buy it on principle.

lis_loc_miradouro.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_miradouro.text: Wind, trams, a view that makes the whole trip feel smaller and bigger at once — like whatever map you had of this tour just got quietly redrawn without asking permission first.

lis_loc_miradouro_breathe.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_miradouro_breathe.text: For five minutes, nothing is due and no one needs you. The list of things that usually matter gets quietly, temporarily shorter.

lis_loc_miradouro_sketch.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_miradouro_sketch.text: The lines come out crooked. You keep the page anyway.

lis_loc_market.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_market.text: Bells, frying dough, a stranger selling cassette tapes of a band nobody's heard of.

lis_loc_market_tape.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_market_tape.text: The tape is warped and wonderful. You'll never find out who they were.

lis_loc_market_watch.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_market_watch.text: A hundred small lives happening at once, none of them checking a set time.

lis_rel_mira.speaker: mira
lis_rel_mira.text: "What if they came for someone else's band?" Mira asks the window, not you. Whoever she pictured up there tonight, she's fairly sure it wasn't this version of her.

choices.label: She's wrong, and you know it
Let her sit with it a moment

lis_rel_mira_a.speaker: mira
lis_rel_mira_a.text: She doesn't argue back this time. That's new — usually she'd deflect a compliment like it cost her something to keep.

lis_rel_mira_b.speaker: mira
lis_rel_mira_b.text: "Okay," she says, eventually. Not fixed. Heard.

lis_rel_theo.speaker: theo
lis_rel_theo.text: "I could sleep for a year," Theo says, "and still be tired when I woke up." It's not the tour talking. It's the last time he felt this tired, and where that ended up.

choices.label: One more pass at the bridge, then rest

lis_rel_theo_a.speaker: theo
lis_rel_theo_a.text: He actually naps. You stand guard over the silence like it's precious — like the alternative is something worth guarding against.

lis_rel_theo_b.speaker: theo
lis_rel_theo_b.text: The bridge is tighter now. Theo looks a little more hollow for it — not frustrated anymore, just quiet in the specific way that isn't calm.

lis_rel_jun.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun.text: "What if the chorus just... stopped," Jun says, "and let the room fill it in?"

lis_rel_jun_a.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun_a.text: "Tonight, then," Jun says, already humming the gap.

lis_rel_jun_b.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun_b.text: Jun shrugs, unbothered. There will be other rooms.

lis_loc_docks.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_docks.text: Fishing boats rock against worn pilings. The water holds the last orange light long after the sky's given it up.

choices.label: Write a line in your notebook

lis_loc_docks_watch.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_docks_watch.text: A fisherman nods at you like you've always been here. You nod back like it's true.

lis_loc_docks_write.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_docks_write.text: One line becomes four. You cross out two and keep the rest.

lis_loc_azulejo.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_azulejo.text: Past closing time, a painter still bends over unglazed tile, brush loaded with cobalt blue. She doesn't look up when the bell rings.

choices.label: Buy a cracked reject tile, cheap

lis_loc_azulejo_watch.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_azulejo_watch.text: Six hundred years of the same nine patterns, she says, and nobody's bored of them yet. You believe her.

lis_loc_azulejo_buy.speaker: narrator
lis_loc_azulejo_buy.text: The crack runs straight through the pattern's center. She wraps it anyway, like the flaw is the whole point.

lis_rel_rowan.speaker: rowan
lis_rel_rowan.text: "Nobody looks at the bass player in a room this pretty," Rowan says, watching the water instead of you.

lis_rel_rowan_a.speaker: rowan
lis_rel_rowan_a.text: Rowan doesn't answer. Just leans a little closer to the rail, and to you.

lis_rel_rowan_b.speaker: rowan
lis_rel_rowan_b.text: "Make them," Rowan repeats, testing the shape of it. "Yeah. Okay."

lis_rel_jun2.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun2.text: "Everything here already sounds finished," Jun says, frustrated. "How do you innovate on top of a thousand years?"

choices.label: You don't have to top it. Just answer it.

lis_rel_jun2_a.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun2_a.text: Jun goes quiet, turning that over. "Answer it," they repeat, like a key turning.

lis_rel_jun2_b.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun2_b.text: Jun grins, already humming a fado melody bent sideways into something new.

lis_rel_mira_letter.speaker: mira
lis_rel_mira_letter.text: A letter caught up with the tour today. "My sister wrote asking if we've 'made it' yet," Mira says. "I don't know how to answer that without sounding like I sold something."

choices.label: Maybe 'made it' just means still here
Don't answer yet. Sit with the question first.

lis_rel_mira_letter_a.speaker: mira
lis_rel_mira_letter_a.text: She writes that back, word for word. It feels truer typed out than it did spoken.

lis_rel_mira_letter_b.speaker: mira
lis_rel_mira_letter_b.text: She folds the letter into her notebook instead, unanswered. "Later," she says. "When I actually know."

lis_rel_mira_letter_fallback.speaker: mira
lis_rel_mira_letter_fallback.text: Mira mentions a letter from home, then changes the subject fast, folding it away before you can ask.

lis_rel_theo_why.speaker: theo
lis_rel_theo_why.text: "I quit for eight months, after the last band," Theo says, quiet. "This tour is me finding out if I can do this without it wrecking me again."

choices.label: How's it going so far, honestly?
I'll watch for it, if you want me to

lis_rel_theo_why_a.speaker: theo
lis_rel_theo_why_a.text: "Better than I expected," he admits, surprised by his own answer. "Ask me again down the road."

lis_rel_theo_why_b.speaker: theo
lis_rel_theo_why_b.text: Something in his shoulders drops. "Nobody's offered that before," he says. "Yeah. Please."

lis_rel_theo_why_fallback.speaker: theo
lis_rel_theo_why_fallback.text: Theo mentions the last band, briefly, then waves it off. "Old story. Not worth telling yet."

lis_rel_jun_why.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun_why.text: "I turned down a touring slot with a band that already had three hit singles," Jun says. "Everyone thought I was insane. I just couldn't watch myself play the same set for two years straight."

choices.label: Was it worth it, though — really?
You clearly don't regret it. That's the answer.

lis_rel_jun_why_a.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun_why_a.text: "Ask me on a good night versus a broke one," Jun laughs. "Tonight, though — yeah. Worth it."

lis_rel_jun_why_b.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun_why_b.text: Jun goes quiet, surprised. "Huh. Yeah. Guess I don't." A real smile, not the performed one.

lis_rel_jun_why_fallback.speaker: jun
lis_rel_jun_why_fallback.text: Jun mentions turning down some old offer, then waves it off. "Old news. Ask me later."

lis_preshow.speaker: narrator
lis_preshow.text: Soundcheck's done. The room is filling. Tonight's shape is still yours to choose.

lis_aftershow.speaker: narrator
lis_aftershow.text: The last chord fades into applause that doesn't want to stop.

choices.label: Head back to the bus early

lis_aftershow_cassette.speaker: narrator
lis_aftershow_cassette.text: Backstage, someone finds a cassette deck older than the whole band combined. You play the warped market tape once, just to hear what nobody else ever will again.

choices.label: Head back to the bus early

lis_aftershow_a.speaker: narrator
lis_aftershow_a.text: Inês buys the band a round, still impressed by how fast the gear came up those stairs. Someone else's tab, gladly.

lis_aftershow_a_generic.speaker: narrator
lis_aftershow_a_generic.text: Someone buys the band a round they can't really afford. Worth it.

lis_aftershow_b.speaker: narrator
lis_aftershow_b.text: The bus is quiet and dark and exactly what you needed.

lis_journal.speaker: narrator
lis_journal.text: You write: Lisbon smelled like rain and someone else's song. You wonder if the promise still counts when the person it was made to never hears how it turned out — then decide it counts more, not less. Onward.

lis_journal_generic.speaker: narrator
lis_journal_generic.text: You write: Lisbon smelled like rain and someone else's song. Onward.
